import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The **Evaluation** dock tab (`?tab=evals`) supports current protocol launch, run detail,
official grading, comparison and reproducible export. Current generation uses the
committed protocol's runtime, model, payer and budgets. Imported historical runs
remain visible with their evidence class; their old arm names do not define a new
current study. The complete prerequisites and request shape are maintained in
`benchmarks/README.md` under **Current launch prerequisites and verification**.

The tab id `'evals'` and its sidebar metadata (label **Evaluation**, Trophy
icon) are **declared** in `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvShell.tsx`;
the `AdvEvalsTab` component is **routed** in
`apps/operator-vite/src/routes/adv/index.tsx` (the `renderAdvTab` switch — `case
'evals': return <AdvEvalsTab />`). The component itself lives at
`apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvEvalsTab.tsx`; the shared viz helpers +
the validity module are under `apps/operator/app/eval-viz/` (imported via the
`@/app` alias).

<Aside type="note" title="Verify in the Tauri shell, never a browser">
The Evaluation UI is part of the desktop app. Drive it through the running Tauri
shell (`cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` → the Evaluation tab), per
[testing](/internal/docs/testing) — not a browser against `:3055`/`:3070`.
</Aside>

## The two stores (why there are two)

- **Operational run store** — `bench_runs` / `bench_run_tasks` / `bench_run_events`
  (migration 296). MUTABLE, lifecycle-driven (`pending → running → grading → done
  | error | cancelled`), lenient while in-flight. This is the live source the UI
  reads via `@papercusp/sync` (`evals.benchRuns`, `evals.benchRun`,
  `evals.benchRunLive`). Preserved file-dir runs are imported one-way (dir → store).
- **Reproducibility cards** — `benchmark_rollout` / `benchmark_run_result` /
  `benchmark_fleet_run` (migrations 291–293). IMMUTABLE, firewall-gated
  (`prereg_hash`), for PUBLISHED graded results. Distinct concern — a live run
  exists long before any reproducibility card.

## Subtabs

| Subtab | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Launch** | Select an isolated workspace, committed protocol, current arm and registered seed. Review the account/runtime readiness, frozen controls and payer-specific usage estimate before launch. |
| **Preserved runs** | Browse runs (imports + live) — id · arm · resolved% · status. Per-run: Grade, Export, Re-run, Delete. Validity badges, live fleet panel, coordination timeline. |
| **Compare** | Arm-vs-arm over the same task set: resolved% delta + Frontier + per-task table + the honest-caveats panel. |

## Launch a current run

The form posts to `POST /api/external-bench/runs/launch` through the maintained
`run-launcher.ts` engine. Select a committed protocol ID, isolated benchmark
workspace, registered arm and seed. `papercusp` selects current su; `baseline`
selects the stock native Codex arm. The protocol fixes the model, effort, task
assignments, concurrency, caps and single registered suite. A historical arm or
configured model alias is not measured current execution identity.

Before launching:

1. Select the current-build route with
   `dev:pipeline_position { path: "packages/operator-core/lib/external-bench/current-su.ts", testClass: "operator-api" }`
   and verify its serving source. Ordinary acceptance uses that build; final
   shipment needs separate proof of the exact green release artifact.
2. Register the account in the isolated benchmark workspace and match its
   credential to the protocol's payer. An ambient account in another workspace
   does not satisfy this prerequisite. Subscription usage is labelled
   **list-price-equivalent**; API-key usage is metered spend. The estimate and
   approval must retain the matching cost basis and authorized ceilings.
3. Calibrate the actual native client and loaded model/runtime on non-study work,
   freeze the permitted inputs with `preregister()`, and verify the introducing
   commit with `requireCommittedPreregistration()` before study generation.
4. Select the protocol's arm and registered seed. The estimate checks the
   committed protocol, account and loaded host; missing or inconsistent evidence
   keeps launch unavailable. The request's observed workspace and units must
   identify the actual execution host. JSON fields cannot create host authority.
5. Launch one registered arm/seed at a time and retain its managed run ID.
   Admission is not a completed run or an official grade. A second attempt of the
   same arm/seed is refused; changing the protocol requires a new preregistration.

Use the complete request and payer-specific prerequisites in
`benchmarks/README.md`; the current form derives launch controls from that
protocol. The former `hive-realqueen`, `fifo-noqueen` and `mini-swe-agent` workflow
is historical context, not the current launch recipe.

At terminal state reconcile the run's task/session/request population, measured
execution identity, provider response and usage evidence, and governor
settlements. Cancellation or restart must retire the run-owned task subtree,
including descendants. Missing accounting keeps efficiency claims closed.

## Monitor live (P-007 / P-008 / P-009)

Run detail reads `evals.benchRunLive` and displays recorded progress and usage.
Historical fleet runs can also expose these older pot-scoped diagnostics from
`spawned_agents` / `agent_usage_samples`; they do not prove a current native
execution matches its protocol:

- **Mug survival** — alive / age / reclaims.
- **Cup status** — placed / working / done / evicted / failed.
- **Per-task progress**, cumulative spend, wall-clock.
- **Coordination timeline** — placements, evictions, recoveries, wakes, event by event.

### Historical fleet validity badges (D-003)

The historical fleet validity model uses red/green badges (`computeValiditySignals` returns
**seven**, in order): `OPUS-ONLY`, `MUG-SURVIVAL`, `EMPTY-DIFF`,
`GENERATION-ATTRIBUTED`, `FLEET-CAP`, `SUBSET-SIZE`, `SINGLE-SEED`. A **fail** (a
non-opus leak, a mug reclaim, a 0-work arm, a phantom win) means the run is NOT
a clean result — and the Compare view will refuse to render it as a valid delta.
Warn/unknown are honest caveats, not invalidating. The same function renders the
badges in both the live monitor and the Preserved-runs view.

- **`GENERATION-ATTRIBUTED`** (D-027) guards against **phantom wins**: a
  non-empty, grade-passing diff with `turns=0` AND `cost=0` AND 0 tokens — a
  recovered / re-placed win that would inflate `resolved%` with work the run
  never measured. It **fails** when any resolved task has zero recorded
  generation (`resolvedZeroGen > 0`), so like the other six it gates validity.
  This was the gap that hid two of the m3 wins until the credibility roadmap
  added it.

## Grade (P-010)

**Grade** runs the OFFICIAL `swe_bench_pro_eval` (`--use_local_docker`, jefzda
images) over the run's collected diffs — the proven `_xbench_grade.py` path. It
persists the per-instance resolved map + `resolvedCount`/`resolvedPct`, and is
re-gradeable (`status: grading → done`). Requires the run's on-disk snapshot
(written on launch completion; preserved/imported runs already have it).

Grading is **dispatched by suite** (`runGradeBySuite`): `swe-bench-pro` (the
default) uses the proven `_xbench_grade.py` / `swe_bench_pro_eval` path;
`swe-bench-verified` is a **separate harness that is not installed here** — rather
than mis-grade Verified instances with the Pro images, the grader throws an
actionable `verified_harness_not_installed` error (with the exact install steps).

## Compare arms (P-011 / P-012)

Pick run **A** (baseline) and **B** (treatment) from the matched current protocol.
The view shows the assigned-task outcome, cost/accuracy Frontier and per-task
results. Inspect the evidence class before interpreting a delta: synthetic,
historical and incomplete current evidence are distinct from current measured
evidence. Complete assigned outcomes, committed protocol and matching measured
execution identity are required; even that evidence alone does not establish
superiority. Conditional graded quality is labelled separately, and missing
official grades keep the primary result inconclusive.

- **The validity gate (D-003):** if EITHER arm fails a validity check, the view
  renders **“No valid delta”** + the failing badges — never a fabricated number.
- **Honest caveats (P-012):** auto-surfaced per-arm (opus-leak, empty-diff,
  subset, seed, cap) + cross-arm (task-set mismatch, task-count mismatch,
  cap-asymmetry, spawn-path parity). A delta is never presented cleaner than its
  caveats.

## Export for 3rd-party reproduction (P-013)

**Export** downloads `predictions.json` (`[{instance_id, patch, prefix}]`),
`tasks-sample.jsonl` and a `README.md` with the exact public re-grade command.
The README records primary assigned outcomes, conditional graded quality,
absent attempts and missing grader measurements. Compare those denominators and
the frozen assignments/source hashes with the stored run. A third party reproduces the
resolved verdicts with the public `swe_bench_pro_eval` + public images, with zero
access to our harness — also the shape for a SWE-bench Pro / SEAL leaderboard
submission.

## Verifying changes

- Unit/integration: `run-store`, `run-launcher` (incl. the kill-mid-run hard
  gate), `grade-runner`, `live-state`, `validity`, `export-bundle`, `AdvEvalsTab`.
- Where the code lives: the UI is `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvEvalsTab.tsx`
  (routed in `src/routes/adv/index.tsx`, declared in `src/components/adv/AdvShell.tsx`);
  the shared viz + `validity.ts` are under `apps/operator/app/eval-viz/`.
- A full **live** walkthrough requires the documented installed prerequisites and
  authorized generation/grading budget. Drive the current protocol through the
  Tauri shell, retain the official grader's source/CSV/image receipt, actual
  image-use trace and per-task output, then compare the export with the stored
  run. An export-helper unit test does not reproduce this journey.
- The registered isolated surface check in `benchmarks/README.md` exercises
  unavailable-protocol launch refusal and Compare → Launch with an empty isolated
  database. It starts no benchmark generation. A passing surface check does not
  establish funded launch, official grading, reproduction or shipment.
